1 غَاثَ ٱللّٰهُ البِلَادَ , (S, O, Msb, K,) aor. يَغِيثُ, inf. n. غَيْثٌ, (S, O, Msb,) God watered the country, or countries, with rain. (O, Msb, TA.) And غَاثَنَا He (God) sent down rain upon us. (TA.) And غاث الغَيْثُ الأَرْضَ, (aor. and inf. n. as above, Msb,) The rain fell upon the earth. (S, O, Msb, K.) And غِيثَتِ الأَرْضُ, aor. تُغَاثُ, (S, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. as above, (S, O,) The land was watered with rain. (S, O, Msb, K.) غِيثَ القَوْمُ The people were rained upon; rain fell upon the people [or upon their land]. (TA.) And غِثَنْا مَا شِئْنَا [We were rained upon as much as we desired]: (S, O, Msb, TA:) originally غُيِثْنَا. (TA.) ―
-b2- غاث النَّوْرُ (tropical:) The blossom shone. (O, K, TA.) ＝
-A2- See also 4 in art. غوث.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
